_purpose: Deterministic seed data for scripts/map_attack_techniques.py. Two lookup tables: (1) graph risk-pattern key -> MITRE ATT&CK technique(s), for the 15 algorithmic detectors in scripts/build_graph.py's detect_risk_patterns(); (2) CWE -> CAPEC -> MITRE ATT&CK technique(s), for app-layer weaknesses already named in SKILL.md Sec 11 (SAST Recommendation Agent). This is a curated starter set, not a full import of the authoritative MITRE CAPEC/ATT&CK corpora.
_confidence_note: Every entry is labeled 'confidence': "seed-unverified". Treat these as a reasoned starting point to review, not certified ground truth. Before relying on this at scale, replace/extend this file from the authoritative public sources: MITRE ATT&CK STIX bundles at https://github.com/mitre/cti, and the MITRE CAPEC database/CWE-CAPEC relationships published at https://capec.mitre.org (CSV/XML export). Do this the same way references/cx-presets-queries/9.7.0_All_queries_by_preset_list.csv is a real vendor export rather than a hand-typed table -- this file should eventually be replaced the same way.
_usage_note: Not every finding maps cleanly onto MITRE ATT&CK. ATT&CK models post-compromise adversary behavior (infrastructure, cloud, identity, containers); many app-layer logic weaknesses (e.g. BOLA, business-logic abuse) have no good 1:1 Enterprise technique and are better described with CWE + CAPEC alone. Entries below with "attack_techniques": [] and a "why_no_attack_technique" field are intentional -- do not force an ID onto them.

unknown_authorization_on_api_call.why_no_attack_technique: Object/function-level authorization gaps (BOLA/BFLA) are an application-logic weakness with no clean 1:1 Enterprise ATT&CK technique. Cite CWE-862/CWE-863 and CAPEC-1 instead (see cwe_to_capec below).

attack_techniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files

frontend_bypasses_gateway_to_internal_se.why_no_attack_technique: This is a control-architecture gap (bypassing a centralized gateway's authN/Z, rate limiting, monitoring), not an attacker technique in itself. If authentication is also missing on the direct path, see unauthenticated_trust_boundary_crossing / CAPEC-115 instead.

attack_techniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain

logging_system_receives_sensitive_data.why_no_attack_technique: Sensitive data landing in logs is an information-disclosure weakness (CWE-532), not a distinct adversary technique, unless the logged data is itself credentials -- in that case treat it like secret_used_outside_managed_store (T1552).

capec: CAPEC-221 Data Serialization External Entities Blowup (closest published pattern to XXE; verify against capec.mitre.org)
CAPEC-1 Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs

CAPEC-1.why_no_attack_technique: Application-layer ACL-bypass pattern; no clean Enterprise ATT&CK equivalent.

CAPEC-62.why_no_attack_technique: CSRF is a client-trust weakness exploited via social engineering of the victim's browser session, not a distinct infrastructure-level ATT&CK technique.

attack_techniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files

CAPEC-586.why_no_attack_technique: Insecure deserialization is an exploitation primitive, not itself a tactic-level adversary technique; it typically enables T1190 or T1059 depending on what the gadget chain achieves.
